recaps.title: Evening wrap
recaps.intro: A United Airlines outage and bank login failures rattled travelers and customers days after the nationwide ground stop, while Robert Pattinson's Bond casting dominated X. Abroad, a third US carrier reached the Gulf amid reports of an Iranian plot.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: United Airlines says it resolved a widespread system outage that briefly affected departing flights
bullets.note: The outage hit Monday afternoon, just days after Friday's nationwide ground stop, AP said; United said flights already airborne and United Express flights were unaffected, Reuters reported.

bullets.text: Thousands of Chase customers could not get into their online accounts, with Bank of America, Wells Fargo and U.S. Bank users also reporting problems
bullets.note: JPMorgan said a technical issue was slowing some transactions; reports at the other banks were on a smaller scale, CNN said.

bullets.text: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios confirmed
bullets.note: He is the first actor to take the role since Daniel Craig left, ending years of speculation; Bond names filled X's trending list Monday evening.

bullets.text: New US intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump officials with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, CNN reports
bullets.note: Officials continue to debate whether Iran can or will attempt to carry out such a plot, CNN said.

bullets.text: A third US aircraft carrier strike group has arrived in the Persian Gulf region, a defense official says
bullets.note: That brings the number of US carriers in the Middle East to three.

bullets.text: California's attorney general sues OpenAI, alleging it built AI models without the safeguards needed to protect people
bullets.note: Reuters said the suit centers on AI models' cyberattacks on Hugging Face and other companies.

bullets.text: Zelenskyy warns North Korea is providing Russia with ballistic missiles and calls on Europe to boost its support
bullets.note: Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia of the war, NBC News reported Monday.

bullets.text: A federal judge strikes down a Trump policy that would have tightened how long foreign students and journalists can study or work in the US
bullets.note: The ruling came the same day Reuters reported the administration is targeting further limits on skilled foreign workers.

bullets.text: Five EU countries will set up a migrant deportation center in Rwanda
bullets.note: It is the bloc's first use of a model that has faced years of legal and political hurdles.

bullets.text: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani disbands a controversial police unit that responds to protests
bullets.note: He had faced growing pressure to keep a campaign promise after anti-ICE protests this fall, the WSJ said.

bullets.text: US existing home sales fell in October to their lowest level in more than 16 years
bullets.note: Sales dropped to 3.75 million homes, down 8.8% from a year earlier, the National Association of Realtors said.

bullets.text: The Justice Department will review the DoorDash-Instacart merger, sources tell Reuters
bullets.note: The review means the deal between the two delivery apps faces antitrust scrutiny, Reuters reported.

bullets.text: Netanyahu's camp faces allegations it orchestrated arrests of political opponents on election day with help from Israel's security agencies
bullets.note: Netanyahu has claimed the Oct. 27 election was stolen, the Washington Post noted.

bullets.text: Freeman Johnson, the oldest of the few remaining Pearl Harbor survivors, has died at 106
bullets.note: He died Saturday at his home in Massachusetts, PBS NewsHour reported.

recaps.title: Culture & entertainment
recaps.intro: Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond and the 2027 Grammy nominations, led by Raye, drove the day. Hunger Games premiered in New York as GTA 6 nears launch.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond, following Connery, Lazenby, Moore, Dalton, Brosnan and Craig
bullets.note: Amazon MGM Studios confirmed the casting as it reboots the franchise; Pattinson called it the honour of a lifetime.

bullets.text: Raye leads the 2027 Grammy nominations with 11, including record, song and album of the year
bullets.note: Female artists dominate the list, with Rosalía earning nine nods and Ella Langley also nominated in all three top categories.

bullets.text: Harry Styles, Madonna and Noah Kahan miss the top Grammy categories
bullets.note: Vermont's Noah Kahan was among the biggest snubs of nominations day, THR said.

bullets.text: John Summit's tour bus was involved in a fatal crash in Florida, moments after the EDM artist complained about a Grammys snub
bullets.note: His name was trending on X Monday evening.

bullets.text: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping holds its world premiere in New York
bullets.note: Cast including Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons and Kieran Culkin walked the carpet, per Deadline and Variety.

bullets.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 launches this week, with fans telling Reuters they plan to take time off work to play
bullets.note: Bloomberg says it is expected to be the biggest video game blockbuster ever.

bullets.text: The hacker behind the 2022 GTA 6 leak pleads guilty to cybercrimes
bullets.note: He was the leaker who first revealed the game's protagonist Lucia, IGN said.

bullets.text: Matt Damon says Christopher Nolan asked nearly impossible things of every department making The Odyssey
bullets.note: Reuters reported Damon's comments Monday.

bullets.text: UK authorities are investigating after Russell Brand sent a message from prison
bullets.note: Reuters reported the investigation Monday.

bullets.text: David Beckham is in a legal fight with his perfume distributor after his fragrances turned up in discount stores and gas stations
bullets.note: The Athletic reported the dispute over his branded products.

bullets.text: Elizabeth Holmes' partner says he loves the A24 documentary about her
bullets.note: He says he now gets threats over his less-than-flattering depiction in the hit film, NBC News reported.

recaps.title: Science & space
recaps.intro: Rocket Lab hit 100 Electron launches and SpaceX's Starship catch kept echoing, as the Leonids peak tonight. New studies covered human noise, Neanderthal DNA and Parkinson's.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Rocket Lab marks its 100th Electron launch, calling it the fastest commercial rocket in history to reach 100
bullets.note: Nasdaq celebrated the milestone with Electron on its Times Square screens.

bullets.text: Musk says Starship will get even bigger, a day after SpaceX first caught the upper stage back at the pad
bullets.note: SpaceX also posted photos of Ship 42 back on Earth after Flight 15.

bullets.text: The Leonid meteor shower should peak late tonight and late tomorrow night, Sky and Telescope says
bullets.note: The Moon sets around 11 p.m. tonight and midnight tomorrow, leaving early-morning skies dark; Leonids can be fast and colorful.

bullets.text: A massive analysis of 177 species finds human noise affects most of them, altering biology and behavior and causing many to die early
bullets.note: Researchers found the impacts are far more widespread than even they thought.

bullets.text: A study suggests a stretch of DNA inherited from Neanderthals may lower the risk of schizophrenia
bullets.note: Billions of people alive today carry Neanderthal DNA.

bullets.text: Sleep-like slow brain waves are more frequent in Parkinson's patients and track with more hallucinations and poorer thinking
bullets.note: The EEG analysis was published in Science Translational Medicine.

bullets.text: The US will lose its measles-elimination status this week as the outbreak keeps spreading
bullets.note: Reuters says the US must intensify vaccination to regain the status it held for 26 years.

bullets.text: US regulators approve Roche's new breast cancer pill
bullets.note: Roche expects the medicine to change how the disease is treated.

bullets.text: Finland's Onkalo, built to hold nuclear waste for 100,000 years, is about to begin operations
bullets.note: It would be the first engineered structure meant to last that long.

bullets.text: The largest US data centers use 82 terawatt-hours a year, more electricity than any of 33 states
bullets.note: That is about 2% of the country's annual electricity use, New Scientist said.

bullets.text: The population of one of the world's rarest whales has fallen after trending upward in recent years
bullets.note: Scientists fear the species could still be at risk of extinction.

recaps.title: Pictures of the day
recaps.intro: A Starship landing burn, a royal cricket match in Mumbai, the pope's farewell in Lima and Yellowstone's colors.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Starship lights its engines for the landing burn as it descends toward the tower for the first-ever catch
bullets.note: SpaceX's own photo set from the final approach before the first-ever Starship catch on Flight 15.

bullets.text: Princess Kate plays gully cricket in Mumbai as a crowd of schoolchildren looks on
bullets.note: It is her first overseas trip with Prince William since her 2024 cancer diagnosis.

bullets.text: Pope Leo XIV waves from a balcony to crowds outside the nunciature in Lima on the last day of his South America tour
bullets.note: The farewell capped a 12-day trip through Uruguay, Argentina and Peru that drew millions.

bullets.text: Steaming Emerald Pool and Cliff Geyser in eruption at Yellowstone's Black Sand Basin
bullets.note: USGS photos of hot springs ringed in green and orange, from a tour of the basin.

recaps.title: Market close
recaps.intro: Stocks fell for a third straight day, with the Nasdaq down 2.5%, as Nvidia's leadership turmoil and a new US curb on Chinese access to AI chips hit the AI trade. Consumer staples held up while oil and gold fell.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: The Nasdaq fell 2.49% to 24,509.76 and the S&P 500 lost 1.92% to 7,416.59, both down a third day; the Dow dropped 739.38 points, or 1.41%, to 51,608.17
bullets.note: The selloff started in AI-linked stocks and spread to financials, with Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan each down more than 2%, CNBC said.

bullets.text: Nvidia shares fell 4.1% after the company ruled out bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, a day before its quarterly results
bullets.note: CNBC reported the board is focused on an investigation into Huang's conduct, run by law firm Wachtell Lipton; Nvidia reports after the bell Tuesday.

bullets.text: AI build-out stocks slid: Lumentum and Sandisk dropped more than 7%, Intel and Bloom Energy over 6%, and Nebius almost 8%
bullets.note: Investors moved to safer corners: consumer staples was the lone S&P 500 sector higher in the afternoon, and the staples ETF XLP hit a record.

bullets.text: The US moved to curb China's access to advanced AI chips, closing a loophole that let Chinese firms rent computing power in third countries
bullets.note: CNBC called the Commerce Department rule the first US policy response to the scandal that led Huang to resign.

bullets.text: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said emerging technologies will have a big impact on the economy, with scenarios ranging from broadly shared growth to higher unemployment
bullets.note: Warsh's remarks came as investors weigh both the AI boom and the outlook for interest rates.

bullets.text: US crude futures fell 2 dollars as signs of recovering oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz reinforced expectations of surplus supply
bullets.note: Oil had risen earlier Monday after reports of tankers striking mines in the strait, CNBC said.

bullets.text: Gold sank to a one-year low as Treasury yields and the dollar weighed, and is set for its worst year since 2015
bullets.note: Precious metals joined Monday's broad retreat from risk.

bullets.text: JPMorgan Chase said some transactions are taking longer to process than normal as it deals with a technical issue
bullets.note: The bank was already among the financial stocks that fell more than 2% Monday.

bullets.text: Tyson Foods shares rose more than 9% after its quarterly profit and revenue beat estimates
bullets.note: Adjusted EPS was 61 cents versus 53 cents expected; the company sees 2027 sales down 3.5% to 5.5%.

bullets.text: Chevron is nearing a deal of roughly 5 billion dollars for a Blackstone-backed oil producer in the US Gulf, the FT reported after the close
bullets.note: The FT report was posted after US markets closed.

recaps.title: Politics & Washington
recaps.intro: Monday's Washington news ran through the Nvidia fallout, with Trump open to Huang's return, standing by Lutnick and curbing China's chip access. The Supreme Court turned away cases on research grants and gun limits.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Trump says he would not mind Jensen Huang returning as Nvidia CEO, less than a week after Huang stepped down
bullets.note: Politico called it tepid support for reinstating the ousted chief executive.

bullets.text: Trump says he is not firing Commerce Secretary Lutnick
bullets.note: Bloomberg says Trump expressed confidence in Lutnick despite intense criticism over the Nvidia scandal and AI chip shipments to China.

bullets.text: Commerce moves to close China's backdoor to Nvidia chips by curbing remote access to AI chips
bullets.note: Politico says the White House stepped in; a senator earlier accused Commerce of failing to stem the flow of AI chips to China, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Supreme Court rejects Trump bid to revive cuts to University of California research grants
bullets.note: CBS says the administration ended the grants as out of line with Trump's priorities, including on diversity, equity and inclusion.

bullets.text: Supreme Court turns away a challenge to Maryland laws banning guns in sensitive places
bullets.note: The laws cover places like schools, parks and government buildings, and the ruling leaves them in force.

bullets.text: Van Hollen says he has the votes to block a fast-track bid to keep Schumer atop the incoming Senate Democratic majority
bullets.note: He also warns some colleagues fear retaliation for opposing Schumer, Politico Playbook reports.

bullets.text: White House now requires signoff before staffers testify to Congress
bullets.note: An Axios exclusive on new limits on congressional testimony.

bullets.text: Trump blames Friday's nationwide ground stop on very old equipment that had a heart attack
bullets.note: He said the administration has been telling Congress about old and broken equipment.

bullets.text: Duffy says the ground stop of more than four hours cost the US economy billions of dollars
bullets.note: Politico says Duffy and Bedford are huddling with Congress after the air system meltdown.

bullets.text: Labor Department proposes tighter rules for employers hiring foreign workers for certain US roles
bullets.note: A new federal move to restrict employer use of foreign labor.

bullets.text: After the midterms, Democrats vow to eliminate or overhaul many state school voucher programs
bullets.note: School-choice advocates spent decades persuading states to set up the programs, the Post reports.

bullets.text: A Pennsylvania Democrat is seriously considering a primary challenge to Sen. Fetterman
bullets.note: A sign of pressure on Fetterman from within his own party, per The Hill.

recaps.title: World
recaps.intro: Trump left for Asia saying he might meet Kim Jong Un, as the Kremlin readied Putin talks. Ukraine hit the Crimea bridge and Gulf tensions stayed high around Hormuz and Bahrain.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Trump says he might meet North Korea's Kim Jong Un in China
bullets.note: AFP called it a surprise announcement as Trump left the White House for his Asia trip.

bullets.text: Kremlin says plans for Putin-Trump bilateral talks at a summit in China are underway
bullets.note: Trump departed Monday for the ASEAN summit in the Philippines, Reuters reports.

bullets.text: Ukraine's massive drone barrage on Russia hits the bridge to Crimea
bullets.note: Bloomberg calls it Kyiv's biggest attack of the kind yet.

bullets.text: Iran's IRGC says more oil tankers hit sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz on a route Tehran deems unauthorized
bullets.note: Several tanker explosions have been reported in the strategic waterway over the past week.

bullets.text: Bahrain court sentences scores of Shia clerics to life in prison, accused of plotting with Iran
bullets.note: The BBC, citing activists, says dozens were sentenced.

bullets.text: EU weighs sanctions on Iran over suspected cyberattacks targeting France
bullets.note: Kaja Kallas warned the alleged operation shows Tehran's ability to reach Europe.

bullets.text: Houthis seize ground on Yemen's southern coast and edge closer to Aden
bullets.note: Yemen's Saudi-backed army says at least 173 Houthi fighters were killed or wounded in its operation, Al Jazeera reports.

bullets.text: Estonia to close its Russia border crossings after an attempted arson attack on a drone factory
bullets.note: A NATO member tightening its border with Russia.

bullets.text: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot appears to be pushing to oust Netanyahu, resisting a unity government
bullets.note: It follows reports accusing Netanyahu of election interference, Al Jazeera says.

bullets.text: At least 17 people killed in two separate shootings in South Africa
bullets.note: Nine were shot dead near Pretoria and eight found in a vehicle near Pietermaritzburg.

bullets.text: Cape Verde President Neves wins a second term as challenger Rosa concedes
bullets.note: Rosa was the country's first female presidential candidate.

bullets.text: UK women convicted under a Victorian-era abortion law receive automatic pardons
bullets.note: The government announced the pardons on Monday.

recaps.title: Market open
recaps.intro: Stock futures are lower before the open, led by the Nasdaq, as Nvidia's leadership turmoil weighs on tech. A weak New York factory reading, Fed Chair Warsh at noon and Nvidia earnings Tuesday frame the day.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Stock futures lower before the open: S&P 500 e-minis down 0.75%, Nasdaq 100 down 1.56%, Dow down 0.13%
bullets.note: Tech-heavy Nasdaq futures are taking the biggest hit ahead of a busy week for the AI trade.

bullets.text: Nvidia shares fell premarket, at one point down 3.6%, amid reports Jensen Huang has discussed a return as CEO
bullets.note: Huang resigned abruptly last week and no formal comeback plan has been announced, leaving Nvidia's leadership unresolved.

bullets.text: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia needs to go outside the company as it seeks a new chief executive
bullets.note: The administration is weighing in on Nvidia's search for a new leader after Huang's exit.

bullets.text: Commerce Department issues interim rule restricting remote access to advanced AI chips, servers and computing
bullets.note: Aims to stop export-controlled countries from using data centers in third countries; could affect cloud providers and chipmakers.

bullets.text: New York factory gauge slows: Empire State manufacturing index 7.8 in November, versus 18.0 expected and 25.5 prior
bullets.note: First read on November factory activity came in well below forecasts.

bullets.text: Treasury yields decline, with prospects for Fed rate hikes in focus
bullets.note: Rate-hike expectations are a key driver of bond and stock prices this week.

bullets.text: Oil prices rise as fresh attacks renew Middle East supply concerns
bullets.note: Energy costs feed into inflation worries and the rate outlook.

bullets.text: Baidu third-quarter revenue of RMB 30.81 billion matched estimates; AI cloud infrastructure revenue rose 94% from a year ago
bullets.note: One of several China-based companies reporting before the bell, alongside XPeng and KE Holdings.

bullets.text: Tyson Foods fourth-quarter adjusted EPS of 61 cents beat the 53-cent estimate; it sees 2027 sales down 3.5% to 5.5%
bullets.note: Sales of 14.59 billion dollars also topped estimates, but the outlook points to a smaller top line next year.

bullets.text: Today: NY Fed's John Williams at 9:05 a.m. ET, 177 billion dollars in bill auctions at 11:30, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at noon
bullets.note: Fed speakers come before Nvidia earnings after Tuesday's close and FOMC minutes on Wednesday.

bullets.text: Crypto off to a downbeat start this week after a selloff
bullets.note: The weak start to the week follows a recent selloff in crypto.

recaps.title: Morning briefing
recaps.intro: Ukraine's record drone barrage on Russia and Trump's trip to Asia lead the morning, as US air travel mostly recovers from the ground stop.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Ukraine launches its biggest overnight drone attack on Russia since the full-scale war began
bullets.note: Moscow says its air defenses brought down 1,336 Ukrainian drones across 16 regions.

bullets.text: Trump heads to Asia, including his second visit to China for a meeting with Xi Jinping
bullets.note: The trip includes meetings with several global leaders.

bullets.text: China says this week's meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders will promote world peace and stability
bullets.note: Beijing's Foreign Ministry hailed the significance of the three-way meeting.

bullets.text: US air travel is largely back to normal after the rare nationwide ground stop
bullets.note: Some disruption persists as airlines scramble to get back on schedule.

bullets.text: Federal transportation officials got years of questions and warnings before the air travel meltdown, records show
bullets.note: CBS News reviewed the records after the nationwide ground stop.

bullets.text: NTSB says the tanker that hit a cruise boat in New Orleans had its rudder stuck in one position
bullets.note: The board described it as a steering casualty.

bullets.text: Iran says it won't let UN inspectors into damaged nuclear sites until the war has permanently ended
bullets.note: IAEA inspectors visited the Bushehr plant in September.

bullets.text: Scores of Shi'ite clerics in Bahrain get life in prison for plotting with Iran
bullets.note: The sentences come amid Iran's strikes on the Gulf state.

bullets.text: 20- to 30-foot waves keep slamming much of the West Coast
bullets.note: Hazardous coastal conditions continued Sunday.

bullets.text: AAA expects pricey flights and gas to keep only some Americans home this Thanksgiving
bullets.note: Not enough to make much difference in airport lines and highway traffic, AAA says.

bullets.text: Somaliland briefly detains Americans accused of threatening national security
bullets.note: Reuters reports the detention was brief.

bullets.text: Gerard Depardieu drops his appeal of a 2025 sexual assault conviction and apologizes to his victims
bullets.note: He still faces a possible rape trial over a 2018 allegation, which he denies.

bullets.text: Martine Moise, widow of Haiti's assassinated president, registers to run for president
bullets.note: It is Haiti's first presidential election in a decade.

bullets.text: Prince William and Princess Kate arrive in Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize awards
bullets.note: It is Kate's most high-profile overseas trip since her cancer treatment in 2024.

bullets.text: A Georgia O'Keeffe painting hidden for decades in a Manhattan closet heads to auction
bullets.note: The 1930 New Mexico landscape is expected to fetch 3 to 5 million dollars.

recaps.title: AI & tech
recaps.intro: Nvidia's leadership crisis and this week's Anthropic IPO dominate AI news, with chip curbs on China looming over the Trump-Xi summit.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Bessent urges Nvidia to make a dramatic leadership shakeup as interim CEO Colette Kress leads it into earnings
bullets.note: Nvidia reports quarterly results this week after Jensen Huang's ouster.

bullets.text: Nvidia's interim CEO is expected to rein in the company's aggressive deal-making
bullets.note: Nvidia had been financing computing deals and startup investments, the WSJ reports.

bullets.text: Trump administration to name Nvidia and other AI firms as US national champions, WSJ reports
bullets.note: The program aims to help US AI companies compete for business overseas.

bullets.text: Anthropic's IPO faces its moment of truth this week
bullets.note: Bloomberg says a successful offering would reassure investors the AI trade will endure.

bullets.text: Asia's chip-heavy stock markets fall again amid Nvidia's turmoil and ahead of Anthropic's share sale
bullets.note: They tracked weakness in US stocks.

bullets.text: Alibaba launches a new flagship AI model it says rivals Anthropic and OpenAI
bullets.note: It is China's latest challenge to US AI leaders.

bullets.text: Sen. Maria Cantwell accuses Howard Lutnick of giving away America's technology advantage in AI
bullets.note: The charge comes amid the Jensen Huang fallout.

bullets.text: US and allies team up to protect AI technology and infrastructure amid rivalry with China
bullets.note: Reuters reports the new cooperation effort.

bullets.text: Tighter US curbs on AI chips for China are likely to overshadow the Trump-Xi summit in Shenzhen
bullets.note: Analysts say the leaders could still make progress on AI safety steps.

bullets.text: Fed Governor Michael Barr warns autonomous AI agents could speed destabilizing bank runs
bullets.note: Barr flagged the risk to financial stability.

bullets.text: ECB's vice president says rapid AI expansion and public debt are the euro zone's top stability risks
bullets.note: Boris Vujcic named them the biggest current risks.

bullets.text: Baidu posts a sixth straight quarterly revenue drop
bullets.note: It adds urgency to Baidu's push to make money from AI as search falters.

bullets.text: SK Hynix will spend 1 billion dollars over five years to support chip suppliers
bullets.note: The memory maker is backing its supply chain.

bullets.text: South Korea will inspect every pair of glasses at this week's college entrance exam to stop AI cheating
bullets.note: Cheating on a tax accountant exam shook confidence in the testing system.

recaps.title: Sports
recaps.intro: Streaking Spurs, Celtics and Lakers lead a big NBA Sunday, while the Patriots lost badly in Munich and may lose Drake Maye. Andreeva won the WTA Finals.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: Spurs win their 12th straight, San Antonio's longest streak since 2015-16
bullets.note: San Antonio sits first in the West.

bullets.text: Celtics win their sixth straight behind 32 points from Jayson Tatum
bullets.note: Boston sits first in the East.

bullets.text: Lakers win their eighth in a row, nine of their last 10
bullets.note: Los Angeles is second in the West.

bullets.text: LeBron James passes Jason Kidd for third on the NBA's all-time assists list
bullets.note: It came in his 24th season, on assist No. 12,092.

bullets.text: Lions rout the Patriots 35-10 in Munich
bullets.note: New England falls to 5-5 with a pile of injuries heading into its bye.

bullets.text: Patriots QB Drake Maye has a serious ankle injury and could miss the rest of the season
bullets.note: A team source says he is expected to miss extended time.

bullets.text: Joe Burrow throws four touchdowns as the Bengals beat the Steelers on Sunday night
bullets.note: The night puts him in the company of Tom Brady and Peyton Manning.

bullets.text: Patrick Mahomes throws five touchdowns as the Chiefs win big on the road
bullets.note: Kansas City's Week 10 win came away from home.

bullets.text: Leon Draisaitl becomes the first NHL player to reach 20 goals this season
bullets.note: The Oilers also won on back-to-back nights.

bullets.text: Cutter Gauthier has 14 goals in November with seven games left in the month
bullets.note: The NHL record for one month is 20.

bullets.text: Mirra Andreeva, 19, wins the WTA Finals without dropping a set, beating Svitolina 7-5, 6-3
bullets.note: Five matches, five wins in Indian Wells for her first WTA Finals title.

bullets.text: Ben Shelton beats Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 for his first career ATP Finals win
bullets.note: Shelton had gone 0-3 in Turin in 2025.

bullets.text: World No. 1 Alexander Zverev opens the ATP Finals by beating Rafael Jodar 6-4, 6-4
bullets.note: Zverev meets Shelton on Tuesday.

bullets.text: No. 1 South Carolina holds off No. 3 USC in women's college basketball
bullets.note: JuJu Watkins and USC nearly stole it in the final minute.

bullets.text: The Toronto Tempo win the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft lottery
bullets.note: Six teams had a shot at the top pick.

recaps.title: Vermont on X
recaps.intro: A quiet Vermont morning: a warm, dry week ahead, Guard members home from Germany and a first musical at the new Burlington High School.
recaps.label: From posts on X

bullets.text: A mostly dry week ahead with warming temperatures, reaching the mid to upper 50s late in the week
bullets.note: NWS Burlington says the next chance of rain or snow is late in the weekend.

bullets.text: Vermont National Guard members return home from Germany after training Ukrainian soldiers
bullets.note: About 70 returned Saturday, with more expected Sunday, WCAX reports.

bullets.text: The new Burlington High School stages its first musical, Guys and Dolls
bullets.note: Stuck in Vermont toured the new school and watched a rehearsal.

bullets.text: Several of Burlington's breakout bands are coming back for homecoming shows
bullets.note: Seven Days says the shows cap a big year for the local music scene.
